name: sand
summary: Dry loose ground: a path worn through grass, the bank of a river, the packed dirt of a yard.
why: Roughness 0.88. Drier and very slightly less scattering than grass, because sand is
mineral and grass is not, and a wet-looking beach is the standard way this goes wrong.
Depth 0.10, the shallowest ground here. Grains are a fraction of a millimetre and the
relief that reads at a walking distance is the ripple rather than the grain - MU's sheet
draws that ripple as colour, and pushing it as height turns a path into gravel.
Range 0.06, low. Sand is the most uniform ground in the town: it is the same stuff all
the way through, where a meadow is a mixture.
